purpose: Small starter set of research-backed candidates. Not a complete dialect model.

guards: Only for a generic sweetened carbonated beverage.
Do not override a more specific state/city profile.
Do not insert beverages when the concept is absent.
Treat as a tendency, not a categorical rule.
features.notes: Widely documented Midwest lexical tendency; local exceptions exist.

guards: Only for generic rubber-soled athletic footwear.
Prefer a generated local profile before forcing this choice.
Tennis shoes is also common across much of the U.S.; do not treat gym shoes as universal Midwest usage.
features.notes: Grieve et al. report the HDS gym-shoes region as especially Midwestern.

guards: Do not generalize particle with to arbitrary verbs.
Do not use as a generic broad-Midwest marker at subtle intensity.
features.notes: Best-supported with come; related motion verbs show variable acceptance.

guards: Use only with the meaning nowadays/these days in a positive-polarity context.
Use sparingly because production frequency is low and varies within the Midland.
Do not use automatically for Kansas City or St. Louis merely because they are Midland cities.
features.notes: Strongly diagnostic academically, but not high-frequency conversational decoration.

guards: Use only in supported Midland contexts.
Do not use for upper-midwest profiles; research reports strong rejection in much of Minnesota and Wisconsin.
Want + in/out is safer than extending the pattern to arbitrary verb/preposition pairs.
